objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only defines the LIBVALKEY_API visibility macro for symbol export with different compilers.

Struct holding function pointers for the allocator suite used by the library. It encapsulates malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup, and free so callers can substitute custom memory management. Users typically fill an instance with their function pointers and pass it to valkeySetAllocators; the library exposes a global valkeyAllocFns (non-Windows) and vk_* wrappers that dispatch through these pointers. All function pointers must be valid and follow the semantics of their libc counterparts. Unknowns: lifetime/ownership rules for the struct instance passed to valkeySetAllocators are not explicitly documented here; infer that the library copies the function pointers by value.

objects.definition: typedef SSIZE_T ssize_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias mapping Windows SSIZE_T to POSIX-like ssize_t on MSVC builds. Provides a signed size type for byte counts on Windows.

objects.definition: typedef ULONG nfds_t;
objects.description: Typedef for the number of file descriptors used with poll on Windows, mapping to ULONG.

Opaque client context type used by the Valkey C client library. It is referenced to perform networking operations (connect, close, set options). Not defined in this header; actual definition is elsewhere.
Opaque options/configuration type used to configure connection parameters when establishing a Valkey connection. Not defined in this header; actual definition is elsewhere.

POSIX time interval structure used here to specify TCP timeouts. It is not defined in this header and is a system type; included only because it appears in a function signature. Details are platform-provided (typically tv_sec, tv_usec).

Parsing task node used by the protocol reader while constructing a reply. Each task represents a single element (string, integer, array, etc.) with bookkeeping for its type, element count (for containers), index within its parent, a user-created object pointer, a link to its parent task, and user privdata.
Vtable of user-supplied constructors/destructor that the reader invokes to materialize parsed reply objects (strings, arrays, integers, doubles, nil, bool) and to free them.

Stateful protocol parser for Valkey/RESP replies. Manages input buffer, parsing tasks stack, error reporting, limits, and uses a provided valkeyReplyObjectFunctions vtable to instantiate reply objects. privdata is user-controlled context.

objects.definition:
typedef struct valkeyReply {
    int type;                     /* VALKEY_REPLY_* */
    long long integer;            /* The integer when type is VALKEY_REPLY_INTEGER */
    double dval;                  /* The double when type is VALKEY_REPLY_DOUBLE */
    size_t len;                   /* Length of string */
    char *str;                    /* Used for VALKEY_REPLY_ERROR, VALKEY_REPLY_STRING
                                   * VALKEY_REPLY_VERB,
                                   * VALKEY_REPLY_DOUBLE (in additional to dval),
                                   * and VALKEY_REPLY_BIGNUM. */
    char vtype[4];                /* Used for VALKEY_REPLY_VERB, contains the null
                                   * terminated 3 character content type,
                                   * such as "txt". */
    size_t elements;              /* number of elements, for VALKEY_REPLY_ARRAY */
    struct valkeyReply **element; /* elements vector for VALKEY_REPLY_ARRAY */
} valkeyReply;
objects.description: Reply object returned by valkeyCommand/valkeyGetReply representing RESP/RESP3 replies: integers, doubles, strings, verbs, bignums, arrays, and push replies. Caller typically frees with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is configured.

objects.definition:
#ifndef _WIN32
typedef int valkeyFD;
#define VALKEY_INVALID_FD -1
#else
#ifdef _WIN64
typedef unsigned long long valkeyFD; /* SOCKET = 64-bit UINT_PTR */
#else
typedef unsigned long valkeyFD; /* SOCKET = 32-bit UINT_PTR */
#endif
#define VALKEY_INVALID_FD ((valkeyFD)(~0)) /* INVALID_SOCKET */
#endif
objects.description: Platform-dependent file-descriptor/socket handle type used by the library to represent the underlying connection handle.

Connection configuration passed to valkeyConnectWithOptions. Selects connection type and endpoint (TCP, UNIX socket, or existing fd), options bitmask, timeouts, optional user data/destructor, and push callbacks. Use VALKEY_OPTIONS_SET_* macros to populate.

Virtual function table used by valkeyContext to abstract underlying transport/implementation (e.g., socket, TLS). Provides connect/close, async I/O hooks, read/write, timeout setter, and private context cleanup.

Synchronous client connection context: holds socket/fd, flags, buffers, timeouts, addressing info, function table, user data, private transport state, and optional RESP3 push handler. Use valkeyConnect* APIs to create and valkeyFree/valkeyFreeKeepFd to destroy.
Enumeration of supported connection backends: TCP/IP, UNIX domain socket, user-provided file descriptor, and experimental RDMA. Also includes a MAX sentinel.

objects.definition: typedef void(valkeyCallbackFn)(struct valkeyAsyncContext *, void *, void *);
objects.description: Function type for async reply callbacks. Invoked with the async context, a reply object pointer, and user privdata. Exact reply type depends on valkey.h definitions.
Node in a singly-linked list storing a reply callback and its subscription bookkeeping for async operations (regular and pub/sub).
Container tracking a FIFO list of valkeyCallback nodes for regular replies or pub/sub callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef void(valkeyDisconnectCallback)(const struct valkeyAsyncContext *, int status);
objects.description: Function type for disconnect notifications. Called when the async connection is closed due to error or request. Status is VALKEY_OK or VALKEY_ERR.

objects.definition: typedef void(valkeyConnectCallback)(struct valkeyAsyncContext *, int status);
objects.description: Function type for connect notifications. Called when the first write/read event indicates the connection was established. Status is VALKEY_OK or VALKEY_ERR.

objects.definition: typedef void(valkeyTimerCallback)(void *timer, void *privdata);
objects.description: Function type for timer callbacks used by event backends. Parameters are implementation-defined timer handle and user data.

Primary handle for an asynchronous Valkey connection. Wraps the synchronous valkeyContext, error state, application data, event-loop integration hooks, connect/disconnect callbacks, reply queues, addressing info, subscription state, and optional RESP3 push handler. Memory and lifecycle are managed by async API functions in this header.

objects.definition:
typedef void(valkeyClusterCallbackFn)(struct valkeyClusterAsyncContext *,
                                      void *, void *);
objects.description: Function type for async command callbacks. Invoked with the cluster async context, a user-supplied privdata pointer, and the command reply pointer.
Represents a single node in a Valkey Cluster, including addressing info, role (primary/replica), connection handles (sync and async), and bookkeeping for slot ownership and replicas.
Slot range mapping entry, binding an inclusive [start,end] hash slot range to its owning cluster node.
Synchronous client context for interacting with a Valkey Cluster, holding configuration, routing/slotmap, connection timeouts, TLS hooks, and pipelining/request state.
Asynchronous cluster client context embedding a synchronous context, plus async attach hooks and connect/disconnect callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t valkeyClusterNodeIterator[9];
objects.description: Opaque iterator state used to iterate over cluster nodes. Backed by an array of 9 uint64_t values; contents are internal.
Configuration object for creating cluster contexts, carrying initial node list, timeouts, authentication, event hooks, async integration, and TLS initialization callback.

functions.name: valkeySetAllocators
functions.description: Configure the library’s allocation functions. Callers provide a valkeyAllocFuncs struct containing function pointers for malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup, and free. After calling this, the vk_* allocation wrappers will use the provided functions. Returns a valkeyAllocFuncs value (exact meaning not documented here; typically such APIs return the previous configuration, but that is not guaranteed by this header).
requirements: fns must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
All members of *fns (mallocFn, callocFn, reallocFn, strdupFn, freeFn) must be valid function pointers matching the declared signatures.
Provided allocators must obey the expected contracts of their standard counterparts (allocation sizes in bytes, return NULL on failure, etc.) as implied by their types and typical usage.
Callers should ensure any existing allocations are managed consistently with the allocator in effect when they were created.

functions.name: valkeyResetAllocators
functions.description: Reset the library’s configured allocation functions back to the library defaults. Subsequent vk_* allocation calls will use the default allocator set by the library. Intended for restoring the initial allocator configuration after customization.
requirements: May affect how future vk_* calls allocate/free; callers must ensure they free memory with the allocator consistent with when it was allocated.
Thread-safety and timing guarantees are not documented here; callers should avoid racing allocator reconfiguration with concurrent allocations.

functions.name: vk_malloc
functions.description: Allocate a block of memory of length size bytes using the library’s currently configured allocator (inline on non-Windows builds; exported function on Windows). Returns a pointer to the allocated memory on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: size is a size_t specifying the number of bytes to allocate; behavior for size == 0 depends on the configured allocator.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
Memory allocated with vk_malloc must be released with vk_free, using the same allocator configuration in effect at allocation time.

functions.name: vk_calloc
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized storage for an array of nmemb elements of size bytes each using the configured allocator. Includes an explicit overflow check: if nmemb * size would overflow size_t, the function returns NULL.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL (e.g., on allocation failure or detected overflow).
If allocation succeeds, the returned memory must be freed with vk_free.
nmemb and size are size_t values; extremely large values may fail or be rejected by the overflow check.

functions.name: vk_realloc
functions.description: Resize the memory block pointed to by ptr to size bytes using the configured allocator. Semantics are those of realloc for the configured allocator (inline on non-Windows; exported on Windows). Returns a pointer to the new block, which may differ from ptr, or NULL on failure (original block remains valid per realloc semantics).
requirements: ptr should be NULL or a pointer previously allocated by the same allocation family used by vk_* (i.e., compatible with the configured realloc function).
Caller must check for NULL on failure and handle the original pointer according to realloc semantics.
If successful, the returned pointer must later be freed with vk_free.

functions.name: vk_strdup
functions.description: Duplicate a NUL-terminated C string using the configured allocator’s strdup function. Returns a newly allocated copy of str on success, or NULL on failure.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
The returned string must be freed with vk_free.

functions.name: vk_free
functions.description: Free a memory block previously allocated by vk_malloc, vk_calloc, vk_realloc, or vk_strdup using the configured free function (inline on non-Windows; exported on Windows).
requirements: ptr should be a pointer previously returned by the corresponding vk_* allocator, or NULL if the configured free function supports free(NULL) semantics (typical, but allocator-dependent).
Do not pass pointers not obtained from the configured allocator.

functions.name: valkeyNetClose
functions.description: Closes the network connection and related socket resources associated with the given valkeyContext. Use when you are done with the connection or upon errors to release the underlying socket and clean up network state. After closing, further I/O on this context will fail until reconnected.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized valkeyContext pointer.
After calling this function, the context's socket is closed; callers should not perform further network I/O on this context unless it is reconnected.

functions.name: valkeyHasMptcp
functions.description: Reports whether Multipath TCP (MPTCP) support is available on the current system. Returns an integer indicator; specific return values are not documented here.

functions.name: valkeyCheckSocketError
functions.description: Checks the underlying socket for pending connection or I/O errors (e.g., via SO_ERROR) and integrates the result with the context's error reporting. Use to detect and surface socket-level errors on a context.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext associated with a socket (typically connected or in the process of connecting).

functions.name: valkeyTcpSetTimeout
functions.signature: int valkeyTcpSetTimeout(valkeyContext *c, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Configures TCP send/receive timeouts on the context's socket using the supplied timeval. Use to bound blocking I/O operations on the connection.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an underlying socket.
tv should represent a non-negative timeout duration; the exact semantics (read, write, or both) are not specified here.

functions.name: valkeyContextConnectTcp
functions.description: Initiates a TCP connection for the given valkeyContext using the supplied connection options (e.g., address, port, timeouts). May establish either blocking or nonblocking connections depending on options. Intended as the primary TCP connect routine for a context.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized valkeyContext that is not already connected.
options must be a valid pointer to a properly initialized valkeyOptions structure containing the necessary TCP connection parameters. The specific required fields are not specified here.
If using nonblocking mode via options, callers may need to call valkeyCheckConnectDone to complete the connection.

functions.name: valkeyKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables and configures TCP keepalive on the context's socket with the specified interval. Use to detect dead peers over idle connections.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an open/valid socket.
interval should be a positive value; the exact units and platform-specific behavior are not specified here.

functions.name: valkeyCheckConnectDone
functions.description: For nonblocking TCP connects, checks whether the connection attempt on the context has finished. Writes a completion indicator to the 'completed' output parameter.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext whose socket is in a connecting or connected state.
completed must be a non-NULL pointer to an int to receive the result.

functions.name: valkeySetTcpNoDelay
functions.description: Enables TCP_NODELAY (disables Nagle's algorithm) on the context's socket to reduce latency for small writes. Useful for request/response workloads where batching is undesirable.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an open/valid TCP socket.

functions.name: valkeyContextSetTcpUserTimeout
functions.description: Sets the TCP_USER_TIMEOUT option on the context's socket, if supported by the platform. This bounds the time that unacknowledged data may remain in the network before aborting the connection.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an open/valid TCP socket.
timeout must be a non-negative duration; units and valid ranges are not specified here and may be platform-dependent.

functions.name: valkeyReaderCreateWithFunctions
functions.description: Create and initialize a protocol reader that parses RESP-like replies and constructs reply objects using the user-supplied callbacks in fn. Typical usage is to allocate a reader once, then repeatedly feed incoming bytes with valkeyReaderFeed and pull completed replies via valkeyReaderGetReply.
requirements: fn is a pointer to a valkeyReplyObjectFunctions table that supplies allocation/creation callbacks for replies; it should outlive the reader or remain valid for the reader’s lifetime (inferred from usage).
Callers should check the return value for NULL to detect allocation failure (inferred from return type and VALKEY_ERR_OOM constant).
On errors during later operations, r->err and r->errstr indicate the error; callers should not rely solely on function return values.

functions.name: valkeyReaderFree
functions.description: Free a valkeyReader and any internal buffers/resources it holds. After this call, the reader pointer must not be used.
requirements: r must be a reader previously created by valkeyReaderCreateWithFunctions (inferred).
Do not use r after freeing it; passing the same reader to valkeyReaderFree more than once results in undefined behavior (inferred).

functions.name: valkeyReaderFeed
functions.signature: int valkeyReaderFeed(valkeyReader *r, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Append len bytes from buf into the reader’s internal buffer for parsing. Parsed data can then be retrieved with valkeyReaderGetReply. Returns VALKEY_OK (0) on success or VALKEY_ERR (-1) on failure; on error, r->err and r->errstr/errno provide details.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized valkeyReader (created via valkeyReaderCreateWithFunctions).
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory when len > 0 (inferred).
len may be 0 to indicate no new data (inferred).
Caller should check the return value; on VALKEY_ERR, consult r->err (VALKEY_ERR_IO/… constants) and r->errstr or errno (as applicable) for details (from header comments).
Feeding data that decodes to more than maxelements (default VALKEY_READER_MAX_ARRAY_ELEMENTS) or causing protocol errors will set error state (inferred from constants and parser role).

functions.name: valkeyReaderGetReply
functions.description: Attempt to extract the next complete reply from the reader’s internal buffer. On success, stores a user-created reply object (as produced via the fn callbacks) into *reply and returns VALKEY_OK (0). If not enough data is available or on error, returns VALKEY_ERR (-1); error details are in r->err and r->errstr.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized valkeyReader (created via valkeyReaderCreateWithFunctions).
reply should be a valid pointer to a location where a void* can be stored; the stored pointer refers to an object created by the configured reply callbacks (inferred).
Callers should check the return value; on VALKEY_ERR, inspect r->err and r->errstr/errno (from header comments).
Call after providing input with valkeyReaderFeed; calling when no complete reply is available will not produce a reply (inferred).
Ownership and lifetime of the returned reply pointer are governed by the provided valkeyReplyObjectFunctions (e.g., freeObject) (inferred from fn table).

functions.name: valkeyReaderSetPrivdata
functions.description: Macro that sets the user-defined private data pointer on a valkeyReader instance. Implemented as a macro assigning r->privdata = p and casting the assigned pointer to int as the return value. Intended for associating caller-specific context with the reader. Note: this is a macro, not a real function; the return value is the assigned pointer value cast to int and is generally not useful on platforms where pointer size exceeds int.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized pointer to a valkeyReader obtained from valkeyReaderCreateWithFunctions.
p may be NULL or any caller-managed pointer; the reader does not take ownership.
Do not rely on the returned int value for logic or portability; prefer to ignore the return value.
This macro performs direct field assignment; passing an invalid r will cause undefined behavior.

functions.name: valkeyReaderGetObject
functions.description: Macro that returns the current temporary reply pointer stored in r->reply. Useful for accessing the last parsed reply object as constructed by the reply object functions. This is a macro, not a function.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized pointer to a valkeyReader.
The returned pointer may be NULL if no reply has been parsed or available.

The lifetime and ownership of the returned object are defined by the reply object functions provided at reader creation; callers must follow those semantics and should not free it unless their reply factory dictates so.
Only meaningful to call after feeding input (valkeyReaderFeed) and obtaining a reply (valkeyReaderGetReply).

functions.name: valkeyReaderGetError
functions.description: Macro that returns a pointer to the internal error string buffer r->errstr (size 128). Use to inspect the textual description of the last error when applicable. This is a macro, not a function.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized pointer to a valkeyReader.
The returned pointer references an internal buffer owned by the reader; do not modify its contents.
The buffer content is only meaningful when an error has occurred (r->err != 0). When no error has occurred, the content may be empty or unspecified.

functions.name: valkeyReaderCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new protocol reader used to parse RESP replies. Typically used internally, but can be used to feed raw RESP data and extract replies.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller owns the returned valkeyReader pointer and must free it using the corresponding reader/free API from read.h (exact function unknown in this header).
The reader must be used with properly formatted RESP data; feeding invalid data will yield parse errors.

functions.name: freeReplyObject
functions.description: Frees a reply object previously returned by valkeyCommand/valkeyGetReply or created by the reader. Safe to call with a NULL pointer (typical C free pattern; exact behavior not explicitly stated).
requirements: The reply pointer must have been obtained from this library (e.g., valkeyCommand/valkeyGetReply/reader).
Do not free the same reply object more than once.
Do not use the reply after freeing it.

functions.name: valkeyvFormatCommand
functions.signature: int valkeyvFormatCommand(char **target, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a command according to the Valkey protocol using a printf-like format string and a va_list, allocating the result buffer and storing it in *target. Returns the length of the formatted command or a negative value on error.
requirements: target must be non-NULL; on success, *target is set to a newly allocated buffer that must be freed with valkeyFreeCommand.
format must be a valid format string expected by libvalkey; the arguments in ap must match the format specifiers.
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list.
Do not pass a va_list that has already been consumed unless re-initialized.

functions.name: valkeyFormatCommand
functions.description: Formats a command according to the Valkey protocol using a printf-like format string and varargs, allocating the result buffer and storing it in *target. Returns the length of the formatted command or a negative value on error.
requirements: target must be non-NULL; on success, *target is set to a newly allocated buffer that must be freed with valkeyFreeCommand.
format must be a valid format string expected by libvalkey; provided arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: valkeyFormatCommandArgv
functions.signature: long long valkeyFormatCommandArgv(char **target, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a command from an argv-style array (argc/argv/argvlen) according to the Valkey protocol, allocating the result buffer into *target. Returns the length of the formatted command or a negative value on error.
requirements: target must be non-NULL; on success, *target is set to a newly allocated buffer that must be freed with valkeyFreeCommand.
argc must be >= 0; when argc == 0, behavior depends on library semantics (unknown).
argv must point to an array of argc pointers; each argv[i] must be non-NULL unless argvlen[i] == 0 (exact null handling unknown).
If argvlen is non-NULL, it must reference an array of argc lengths giving the length for each corresponding argv[i]; if argvlen is NULL, argv strings must be null-terminated.

functions.name: valkeyFreeCommand
functions.description: Frees a command buffer previously allocated by valkeyFormatCommand/valkeyvFormatCommand/valkeyFormatCommandArgv.
requirements: cmd must be a pointer previously returned in *target by one of the valkeyFormatCommand* functions.
Do not free the same buffer more than once.
Do not use the buffer after freeing it.

functions.name: valkeyConnectWithOptions
functions.description: Creates a new connection using the provided valkeyOptions (TCP/UNIX/user FD, timeouts, flags). Returns a context representing the connection, or NULL on failure.
requirements: options must be non-NULL and properly initialized for the chosen connection type (e.g., VALKEY_OPTIONS_SET_TCP/UNIX or fields set manually).
If options->connect_timeout or command_timeout are provided, they must point to valid struct timeval instances for the duration of the call.
When using TCP, options->endpoint.tcp.ip and port must be set; when using UNIX, endpoint.unix_socket must be set; when using user FD, endpoint.fd must be a valid open descriptor.
Caller owns the returned valkeyContext and must eventually call valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.
If options->free_privdata is set and privdata is provided, ensure the destructor is valid for later cleanup.

functions.name: valkeyConnect
functions.description: Creates a new blocking TCP connection to the given IP/hostname and port. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: ip must be non-NULL and reference a valid address or hostname.
port must be a valid TCP port number (range validation not specified in the header).
Caller must free the returned context with valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: valkeyConnectWithTimeout
functions.signature: valkeyContext *valkeyConnectWithTimeout(const char *ip, int port, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a new blocking TCP connection with a connect timeout. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: ip must be non-NULL and reference a valid address or hostname.
tv specifies the connect timeout; it is passed by value and must contain a valid time interval.
Caller must free the returned context with valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: valkeyConnectNonBlock
functions.description: Creates a new non-blocking TCP connection to the given IP/hostname and port. Returns a context or NULL on failure. The connect may complete asynchronously.
requirements: ip must be non-NULL and reference a valid address or hostname.
Caller must manage the socket for non-blocking I/O (e.g., integrate with event loop) and call valkeyFree/valkeyFreeKeepFd when done.

functions.name: valkeyConnectBindNonBlock
functions.signature: valkeyContext *valkeyConnectBindNonBlock(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Creates a new non-blocking TCP connection, binding the local side to source_addr before connecting. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: ip must be non-NULL; source_addr must be a valid local address string suitable for bind().
Caller must manage non-blocking I/O and free the context when done.

functions.name: valkeyConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse
functions.signature: valkeyContext *valkeyConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Creates a new non-blocking TCP connection, binding to source_addr with SO_REUSEADDR enabled. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: ip must be non-NULL; source_addr must be a valid local address string suitable for bind().
Caller must manage non-blocking I/O and free the context when done.

functions.name: valkeyConnectUnix
functions.description: Creates a new blocking UNIX domain socket connection to the given path. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
Caller must free the returned context with valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: valkeyConnectUnixWithTimeout
functions.signature: valkeyContext *valkeyConnectUnixWithTimeout(const char *path, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a new blocking UNIX domain socket connection with a connect timeout. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
tv specifies the connect timeout and must contain a valid time interval.
Caller must free the returned context with valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: valkeyConnectUnixNonBlock
functions.description: Creates a new non-blocking UNIX domain socket connection to the given path. Returns a context or NULL on failure. Connect may complete asynchronously.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
Caller must manage non-blocking I/O and free the context when done.

functions.name: valkeyConnectFd
functions.description: Wraps an already-open file descriptor/socket in a new valkeyContext. Returns a context or NULL on failure.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open socket/descriptor compatible with the platform-specific valkeyFD definition.

Caller retains responsibility for the lifetime of fd if using valkeyFreeKeepFd; otherwise, freeing the context may close the underlying fd depending on implementation (exact behavior not fully specified here).
Caller must free the returned context with valkeyFree or valkeyFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: valkeyReconnect
functions.description: Reconnects the given context using the same options as the initial connection (host/path, timeouts, bind address, flags unchanged). Returns VALKEY_OK on success or VALKEY_ERR on failure.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext previously connected/initialized with saved connection info.
After reconnection, socket options that were applied directly to the socket (e.g., keepalive) are not automatically re-applied per the general note; reconfigure if needed.
Do not use the context for I/O while reconnection is in progress.

functions.name: valkeySetPushCallback
functions.description: Sets the RESP3 PUSH message callback on a blocking context. Returns the previous callback pointer (or possibly NULL).
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext.
fn may be NULL to clear the callback; behavior when NULL is set is library-defined (not detailed here).
The callback must conform to valkeyPushFn signature and be safe for invocation from the library’s I/O paths.

functions.name: valkeySetTimeout
functions.signature: int valkeySetTimeout(valkeyContext *c, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Sets the per-command timeout on the context. Returns an integer status (VALKEY_OK on success or VALKEY_ERR on failure).
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext.
tv must contain a valid time interval.
This affects synchronous command timeouts and can be updated at runtime.

functions.name: valkeyEnableKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the underlying socket using a default interval. Returns status code.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an underlying TCP socket.
Setting applies directly to the socket and is not automatically re-applied after reconnect; caller must re-enable after valkeyReconnect.

functions.name: valkeyEnableKeepAliveWithInterval
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the underlying socket with a specified interval in seconds. Returns status code.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an underlying TCP socket.
interval should be a positive number of seconds (the default constant is VALKEY_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL; exact valid range not specified).
Setting applies directly to the socket and is not automatically re-applied after reconnect; caller must re-enable after valkeyReconnect.

functions.name: valkeySetTcpUserTimeout
functions.description: Sets the TCP_USER_TIMEOUT option on the underlying socket. Returns status code. The unit for timeout is not specified in this header (commonly milliseconds, but unknown here).
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext with an underlying TCP socket.
timeout must be a non-negative value; exact unit and range are unknown from this header.
Setting applies directly to the socket and is not automatically re-applied after reconnect; caller must reconfigure after valkeyReconnect.

functions.name: valkeyFree
functions.description: Frees a valkeyContext and associated resources, closing the underlying connection. Safe to call with NULL (typical C free pattern; exact behavior not explicitly stated).
requirements: Do not use the context after freeing it.
If a push callback, privdata, or other resources have destructors set in the context/options, they may be invoked during free.

functions.name: valkeyFreeKeepFd
functions.description: Frees the valkeyContext but keeps and returns the underlying file descriptor/socket. Useful for handing off the socket. Caller takes ownership of the returned descriptor.
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext.
After this call, the context must not be used.
Caller becomes responsible for closing the returned valkeyFD.

functions.name: valkeyBufferRead
functions.description: Attempts to read pending data from the socket into the input buffer/reader. Returns status code (non-zero error handling unspecified here).
requirements: c must be a valid valkeyContext.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid NUL-terminated C strings as bytes, suitable for
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() consumers expecting const char* data. It crafts strings that
# exercise interesting Valkey behaviors, especially key hashing/slots and
# vk_strdup usage. No trailing mutations; always valid UTF-8-compatible or
# binary-safe (but without embedded NUL before terminator).

RESP_SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:.{}[]()/|~^$@,#%+="

# Some interesting Redis/Valkey keys and patterns to exercise cluster slot hash tags,
# special characters, numeric forms, and edge cases.
STATIC_INTERESTING: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "a",
    "0",
    "key",
    "Key",
    "KEY",
    "{user}:1",           # hash tag
    "user:{42}",          # hash tag
    "{same_slot}",        # entire key is tag
    "prefix:{same_slot}:x",
    "{a}{b}",             # multiple braces
    "no_tag}",            # unmatched
    "{notclosed",         # unmatched
    "{hash}tail",         # tag with suffix
    "::",                 # separators
    ":0:",
    "🚀unicode",           # utf-8 multi-byte
    "ümlaut",              # non-ascii
    "with space",
    "with\tTab",
    "with\nLF",           # newline inside (no NUL)
    "colon:separated:parts",
    "numeric:18446744073709551615",  # big number
    "-1",
    "+1",
    "0xdeadbeef",
    "key/with/path",
    "key|pipe",
    "key,comma",
    "{slot}{}",           # empty tag then braces
    "{",
    "}",
]

# Ensure no embedded NULs in produced strings.
def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(RESP_SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

# Generate a key that intentionally uses RESP3/cluster-interesting shapes
# including braces for hash tags and mixed bytes, but never NUL.
def _gen_interesting_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        # Use a static seed to hit deterministic behaviors
        s = rng.choice(STATIC_INTERESTING)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        # Build a tagged key: prefix{tag}suffix
        tag = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 16)
        pre = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
        suf = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
        s = f"{pre}{{{tag}}}{suf}"
    else:
        # Random ASCII with punctuation
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64)
        # Occasionally insert braces to trigger hash-tag code paths
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            i = rng.randint(0, len(s))
            j = rng.randint(i, len(s))
            s = s[:i] + "{" + s[i:j] + "}" + s[j:]
    # Add occasional whitespace or special chars (but no NUL)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        inserts = [" ", "\n", "\t", ":", ",", "/", "|"]
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + rng.choice(inserts) + s[pos:]
    # Limit to reasonable length for vk_strdup and cluster hashing
    if len(s) > 1024:
        s = s[:1024]
    return s

# Sometimes provide very long strings to exercise allocation paths, but within 4KiB
# output constraint and avoiding embedded NUL.
def _gen_long(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(256, 2048)
    blocks = []
    while len("".join(blocks)) < length:
        blocks.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 8, 32))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            blocks.append("{" + _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8) + "}")
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            blocks.append(":")
    s = "".join(blocks)[:length]
    return s

# Compose multiple candidate strings into one buffer separated by NUL? No: FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# typically consumes a single blob. We will return a single NUL-terminated string.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide scenario
    mode = rng.choices(
        population=[
            "static",      # pick from curated
            "tagged",      # crafted hash-tag forms
            "random",      # random safe ascii
            "long",        # long allocation
            "unicode"      # utf-8 multi-byte
        ],
        weights=[30, 25, 25, 10, 10],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if mode == "static":
        s = rng.choice(STATIC_INTERESTING)
    elif mode == "tagged":
        s = _gen_interesting_key(rng)
    elif mode == "random":
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 128)
    elif mode == "long":
        s = _gen_long(rng)
    else:
        # Unicode: ensure valid UTF-8 without NULs
        # mix ascii with some code points
        pieces: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)):
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                pieces.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8))
            cp = rng.choice([
                0x00E4,  # ä
                0x00F6,  # ö
                0x00FC,  # ü
                0x03B1,  # α
                0x03C0,  # π
                0x0416,  # Ж
                0x20AC,  # €
                0x1F680, # 🚀
                0x1F600, # 😀
            ])
            pieces.append(chr(cp))
        s = "".join(pieces)
        # Occasionally add hash tag braces around a part
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
            s = s[:pos] + "{" + s[pos:] + "}"

    # Ensure overall size cap and no embedded NULs (should already hold)
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")
    # Encode to UTF-8 for bytes; for pure ASCII this is identity.
    data = s.encode("utf-8")

    # Truncate if needed to keep <= 4096 including terminator
    if len(data) >= 4096:
        data = data[:4095]
        # Avoid cutting in the middle of a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence.
        # Back up to a valid boundary if needed.
        # UTF-8 continuation bytes have top bits 10xxxxxx.
        while len(data) > 0 and (data[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            data = data[:-1]

    # Append NUL terminator for C-string expectations.
    return data + b"\x00"

import random
import struct
import ipaddress

# We need to generate a bytes buffer that, when consumed by the fuzzer, will
# provide interesting values for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (hostname/IP), FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), etc.
# The target stub uses:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() once for opts.endpoint.tcp.ip (must be non-empty hostname/IP)
# - optionally another FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for source address
# - several FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) to choose booleans and port/timeouts
# Our strategy: encode a simple self-describing stream with:
# [count_of_strings][strings...][count_of_uints][uints...]
# Strings are provided as length-prefixed UTF-8 bytes; uints are 32-bit little-endian.
# This format is arbitrary but deterministic and easy for the harness to map.
# The fuzzing harness will likely just read sequentially; by placing values in order,
# the first FUZZ_PARAM_STR gets a valid hostname/IP, subsequent calls get additional
# reasonable addresses; FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) will read from our ints region.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

HOSTNAMES = [
    b"localhost",
    b"example.com",
    b"test.local",
    b"intra.net",
    b"valkey.localdomain",
]

IPV4S = [
    b"127.0.0.1",
    b"192.168.1.1",
    b"10.0.0.1",
    b"172.16.0.2",
    b"8.8.8.8",
]

IPV6S = [
    b"::1",
    b"2001:db8::1",
    b"fe80::1",
    b"2001:4860:4860::8888",
]


def _gen_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(HOSTNAMES)
    elif choice == 1:
        return rng.choice(IPV4S)
    elif choice == 2:
        return rng.choice(IPV6S)
    else:
        # generate random but valid-ish hostname label(s)
        labels = []
        nlabels = rng.randint(1, 3)
        for _ in range(nlabels):
            L = rng.randint(1, 10)
            s = bytearray()
            for i in range(L):
                if i == 0 or i == L - 1:
                    ch = rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789")
                else:
                    ch = rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-")
                s.append(ch)
            labels.append(bytes(s))
        return b".".join(labels)


def _gen_source_addr(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Either empty to encourage nullptr, or a valid IP/hostname.
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # Provide a non-empty alt; sometimes return empty to push nullptr path not via string but via uint toggle
        return _gen_hostname(rng)
    else:
        return _gen_hostname(rng)


def _pack_str(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<I", len(s)) + s


def _gen_uints(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> list[int]:
    uints = []
    # Values to drive interesting branches:
    # - booleans (0/1)
    # - ports (1..65535)
    # - timeouts small values
    for i in range(count):
        kind = rng.randrange(0, 5)
        if kind == 0:
            v = rng.choice([0, 1])
        elif kind == 1:
            # port-ish
            v = rng.randint(1, 65535)
        elif kind == 2:
            # small timeout usec/ms
            v = rng.randint(0, 1000)
        elif kind == 3:
            # larger random
            v = rng.getrandbits(32)
        else:
            # edge-y
            v = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 999, 1000, 65535, 0xFFFFFFFF])
        uints.append(v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return uints


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Plan strings: first is mandatory destination host/IP (non-empty),
    # second optional source address (but stub may or may not use it depending on a uint toggle).
    # We'll provide several extras to ensure availability.
    strings = []
    strings.append(_gen_hostname(rng))
    strings.append(_gen_source_addr(rng))
    # Add a few more candidates
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        strings.append(_gen_hostname(rng))

    # Generate a pool of uints. Stub uses around 7-8 uints; provide more.
    uints = _gen_uints(rng, count=16)

    # Encode: [num_strings][strings...][num_uints][uints...]
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack("<I", len(strings))
    for s in strings:
        out += _pack_str(s)
    out += struct.pack("<I", len(uints))
    for v in uints:
        out += struct.pack("<I", v)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator crafts valid inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used by stubs that
# build Valkey commands via valkeyFormatCommand and valkey*Argv. The fuzzer
# pulls multiple strings from a single buffer; here we encode a small
# self-describing sequence of alphanumeric strings so the harness can slice
# them deterministically.
#
# Encoding layout:
#  - 1 byte: count N (number of strings, 1..8)
#  - Repeated N times:
#      1 byte: length L (0..255)
#      L bytes: ASCII payload (alphanumeric plus selected safe symbols)
#  - Trailing padding: a pool of extra concatenated strings (without header)
#    to allow additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls to still retrieve reasonable
#    substrings if the harness consumes more than N strings.
#
# All data are printable; sizes stay <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
EXTRA_CHARS = SAFE_CHARS + "_-:.@/#"  # permissible extras for keys/values

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, length: int, alphabet: str) -> bytes:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)).encode('ascii')

def _make_interesting_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []
    # Seed with common Redis/Valkey key/value patterns to exercise parser:
    templates = [
        b"key",
        b"value",
        b"foo",
        b"bar",
        b"user:1000",
        b"session:abcdef",
        b"longkey",
        b"short",
    ]
    out.extend(templates)

    # Add randomized sizes including edge-y but valid lengths.
    for L in [0, 1, 2, 3, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255]:
        if L == 0:
            out.append(b"")
        else:
            out.append(_rand_ascii(rng, L, EXTRA_CHARS))

    # A few medium random strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        L = rng.randint(4, 64)
        out.append(_rand_ascii(rng, L, EXTRA_CHARS))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for s in out:
        if s not in seen:
            uniq.append(s)
            seen.add(s)
    return uniq

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = _make_interesting_strings(rng)

    # Choose how many strings to place in the header-driven section (1..8)
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    chosen = [rng.choice(strings) for _ in range(n)]

    # Clamp lengths to 0..255, and for this target keep values <= 256 per stub
    # expectations; we already generate within that bound.

    parts: List[bytes] = []
    parts.append(bytes([n & 0xFF]))
    for s in chosen:
        L = len(s)
        if L > 255:
            s = s[:255]
            L = 255
        parts.append(bytes([L & 0xFF]))
        parts.append(s)

    # Trailing pool: concatenate 10-20 additional strings, each prefixed by a
    # single length byte to allow simple slicing by the harness if it expects
    # further FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls. Not a strict contract, but remains valid
    # printable content if read as raw.
    pool_count = rng.randint(10, 20)
    pool_bytes: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(pool_count):
        s = rng.choice(strings)
        s = s[:255]
        pool_bytes.append(bytes([len(s) & 0xFF]))
        pool_bytes.append(s)

    payload = b''.join(parts + pool_bytes)

    # Ensure maximum size constraint
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]

    return payload

import random
import ipaddress

# Data type: cluster seed address list
# Expected format examples:
#  - "127.0.0.1:6379"
#  - "host1:7000,host2:7001,host3:7002"
#  - IPv6 forms: "[::1]:6379", "[2001:db8::1]:7000,127.0.0.1:7001"
#  - Hostnames, unicode (DNS-like), optional spaces around commas
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for opts.initial_nodes.
# This generator returns bytes representing a seed list string with diverse
# but valid variations to exercise parsing and connection-option code paths.

PORT_DEFAULTS = [6379, 7000, 7001, 7002, 26379]
HOST_TOKENS = [
    "127.0.0.1",
    "localhost",
    "valkey.example.com",
    "cache",
    "node-α",  # unicode
    "srv-☁",   # unicode
]


def _rand_port(rnd: random.Random) -> int:
    # Prefer valid ports; include edge and special ones.
    choices = PORT_DEFAULTS + [1, 9, 80, 443, 1024, 11211, 49152, 65535]
    return rnd.choice(choices)


def _rand_ipv4(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Favor local/private ranges to avoid unintended external networking
    nets = [
        ipaddress.ip_network("127.0.0.0/8"),
        ipaddress.ip_network("10.0.0.0/8"),
        ipaddress.ip_network("192.168.0.0/16"),
        ipaddress.ip_network("172.16.0.0/12"),
    ]
    net = rnd.choice(nets)
    # Avoid network/broadcast by picking from usable range when possible
    hosts = list(net.hosts())
    if not hosts:
        return str(net.network_address)
    return str(rnd.choice(hosts))


def _rand_ipv6(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Favor loopback/link-local/ULA to stay local-ish
    nets = [
        ipaddress.ip_network("::1/128"),
        ipaddress.ip_network("fc00::/7"),
        ipaddress.ip_network("fe80::/10"),
    ]
    net = rnd.choice(nets)
    # For /128, only one address
    if net.num_addresses <= 2:
        addr = net.network_address
    else:
        # pick random host in subnet
        offset = rnd.randrange(0, int(net.num_addresses))
        addr = net.network_address + offset
    return f"[{addr.compressed}]"  # bracketed form for IPv6 with port


def _rand_hostname(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rnd.choice(HOST_TOKENS)
    # Optionally append a numeric suffix or subdomain
    parts = [base]
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(str(rnd.randrange(0, 100)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        sub = rnd.choice(["dc1", "edge", "zone-a", "π"])  # unicode variant
        parts.insert(0, sub)
    name = "-".join(parts)
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        domain = rnd.choice([".local", ".lan", ".example", ".test"])  # non-public
        name += domain
    return name


def _rand_host(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    t = rnd.random()
    if t < 0.4:
        return _rand_ipv4(rnd)
    elif t < 0.7:
        return _rand_hostname(rnd)
    else:
        return _rand_ipv6(rnd)


def _entry(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    host = _rand_host(rnd)
    port = _rand_port(rnd)
    return f"{host}:{port}"


def _make_list(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate between 1 and 6 entries; include variety in separators/spaces
    n = rnd.randint(1, 6)
    entries = [_entry(rnd) for _ in range(n)]

    # Optionally duplicate or reorder to simulate typical user input
    if rnd.random() < 0.3 and n > 1:
        entries[rnd.randrange(n)] = entries[0]
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        rnd.shuffle(entries)

    # Choose separator style and spacing variants
    sep = rnd.choice([",", ", ", ",\t", " , "])  # include space and tab variants
    s = sep.join(entries)

    # Occasionally wrap list in whitespace or newline to exercise trimming
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        pad_left = rnd.choice(["", " ", "\t"]) * rnd.randint(0, 2)
        pad_right = rnd.choice(["", " ", "\t"]) * rnd.randint(0, 2)
        s = f"{pad_left}{s}{pad_right}"

    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one of several patterns, all valid as an initial seed list
    pattern = rnd.randrange(0, 6)

    if pattern == 0:
        # Single localhost/default port
        s = f"127.0.0.1:{_rand_port(rnd)}"
    elif pattern == 1:
        # IPv6 only
        s = f"{_rand_ipv6(rnd)}:{_rand_port(rnd)}"
    elif pattern == 2:
        # Mixed IPv4 + hostname
        s = f"{_entry(rnd)}, {_entry(rnd)}"
    elif pattern == 3:
        # Larger mixed list
        s = _make_list(rnd)
    elif pattern == 4:
        # Hostnames only
        s = ",".join(f"{_rand_hostname(rnd)}:{_rand_port(rnd)}" for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 5)))
    else:
        # Include unicode and edge ports
        s = f"node-☁:{_rand_port(rnd)}, { _rand_ipv4(rnd) }:{_rand_port(rnd)}, {_rand_ipv6(rnd)}:{_rand_port(rnd)}"

    # Ensure output size within 4096 bytes
    b = s.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return b
